items.question: How does reflective awareness of worldly fear arise in the heart through the descent of power?
premises: Fear of worldly existence can produce a trembling touch in the heart.
From that touch reflective awareness of the fear of becoming can arise.
This manifestation occurs through the descent of power.
items.inference: Even a fear-born stirring in the heart can become liberating reflective awareness when empowered by śaktipāta.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of yena is slightly open without the following verse.
items.plain_english: Even from a trembling touch born of fear of worldly existence, a reflective awareness of the fear of becoming can arise in the heart and become manifest through the descent of power.

items.question: In whom does Bhairava become manifest as the power that dries up time?
premises: Some are characterized as drying up the time principle that drives the stars.
Some minds delight in absorption in the devouring of time.
Bhairava becomes manifest in such beings.
items.inference: The Bhairava reality reveals itself in those who transcend or relish the dissolution of time.
uncertainties: The subject prakaṭaḥ is carried over from the surrounding context.
items.plain_english: He becomes manifest in those who dry up the time principle that drives the stars, and in those whose minds delight in absorption in the devouring of time.

items.question: Whose roaring terrifies contracted bound beings within and without?
premises: The goddesses of one's own senses have a roaring.
The fourfold group of khecarī and others operates within and without.
Their roaring is directed toward the fear of contracted bound beings.
items.inference: The terrifying roar belongs to the inner and outer goddess-powers that confront the contracted state of bound beings.
uncertainties: The main predicate is implicit and depends on the surrounding verses.
items.plain_english: Their roaring is for the fear of contracted bound beings—the roaring of the goddesses of one's own senses and also of the fourfold group of khecarī and others, within and without.

items.question: Why is the lord of that group praised as Bhairava in the scripture?
premises: He is the lord of that goddess group.
He is greatly terrifying because he shatters worldly activity.
The teachers praise him in the scripture through etymological meanings.
items.inference: The name Bhairava is affirmed by the teachers as expressing his lordship and his power to break the course of worldly existence.
items.plain_english: The lord of that group, greatly terrifying because he shatters the activity of worldly existence, is praised in the scripture by the teachers as Bhairava through these etymological meanings.

items.question: What qualities characterize Bhairava's play beyond rejection and acceptance?
premises: There is no concern with what should be rejected or accepted.
His state overflows as the mass of his own bliss.
This is expressed as play, supremacy, and autonomy.
items.inference: Bhairava's activity is free play grounded in bliss, supremacy, and absolute autonomy.
items.plain_english: Where there is no talk of what is to be rejected or accepted, there is play as the overflowing mass of one's own bliss, the will to abide in supremacy over all, and likewise autonomy.

items.question: How can all activity and expression be understood as praise of Bhairava?
premises: Activity occurs through difference even in the undivided self.
Articulate expression arises in that differentiated activity.
All manifestation illumines him.
items.inference: Because everything manifests and illumines him, all differentiated activity and speech can be taken as his praise.
items.plain_english: Even in the undivided self, activity appears through difference as articulate expression; and because all manifestation illumines him, everything becomes his praise.

items.question: What is the nature of one's course of action after attaining the self inclined toward Bhairava?
premises: From the attainment of selfhood onward one is inclined toward him.
This inclination extends to everything that is to be done.
That course is awareness, action, and the powers of knowing and doing.
items.inference: After self-attainment, all action proceeds as a unified course of awareness and activity grounded in Bhairava.
items.plain_english: From the attainment of selfhood onward, in everything that is to be done, the course becomes inclined toward him—consisting of awareness, made of all action, and endowed with the powers of knowing and doing.

items.question: Why is the deity remembered as Pati and Śiva who benefits all beings?
premises: The teachers explain the deity through etymological meanings in the Śiva scripture.
He teaches, restrains, protects, and matures.
Through these functions he benefits all.
items.inference: Because his functions are wholly beneficent, he is rightly called Pati and Śiva, and nothing in that reality is non-Śiva.
items.plain_english: Thus, by etymological explanations in the scripture whose body is Śiva, the teachers remember the deity; because he teaches, restrains, protects, and matures, he benefits all. Therefore he is the Lord, Śiva himself consisting of the highest good, and there is nothing there that is not Śiva.

items.question: Why is the qualifier 'supreme and great' applied to the one who removes limitation?
premises: Such a form may shine to some extent in Rudra, Upendra, and others.
The one in question removes limitation.
A supreme and great qualifier is therefore assumed for him.
items.inference: Because his nature surpasses even its partial reflections in other deities, he is designated by the supreme and great state.
uncertainties: The compound analysis of sphuredyena follows the transmitted reading.
items.plain_english: Since such a form may shine even to some extent in Rudra, Upendra, and others, the qualifier 'supreme and great state' is assumed for the one who removes limitation.

items.question: By what authority and method is the true principle to be known presented here?
premises: A true principle to be known is being shown.
It is shown by the command of Śiva.
The presentation proceeds through awareness, reasoning, scripture, and the Trika sequence.
items.inference: The teaching claims legitimacy from Śiva's command and from a fourfold method of realization and exposition.
items.plain_english: Thus, that true principle to be known is shown by me, by the command of Śiva, through one's own awareness, sound reasoning, the Lord's scripture, and the sequence of the Trika.

items.question: How do the three primary powers of that Lord become twelve?
premises: That Lord has three powers beginning with parā.
These powers shine in emission, maintenance, resorption, and the fourth.
Their operation across these four yields twelve.
items.inference: The threefold śakti of the Lord unfolds into a twelvefold manifestation through the four cosmic modes.
items.plain_english: His three powers, beginning with parā, shine in emission, maintenance, resorption, and the fourth; therefore these are declared as twelve.

items.question: Where are worshippers fully established when Śiva is understood in his complete nature?
premises: Śiva is called supreme in this full nature.
This fullness includes the powers just described.
Worshippers are established directly in that reality.
items.inference: True worship culminates in direct establishment in the supreme Śiva whose nature is fully expressed through his powers.
items.plain_english: This one, of such full nature, is called the supreme Śiva; therefore worshippers are directly and fully established right there.

items.question: What explains the many scriptural divisions and arrangements of these powers?
premises: The powers are described with divisions, parts, deficiencies, excesses, and other arrangements.
These descriptions appear in the scriptures.
Their basis is the autonomy of that Lord.
items.inference: All scriptural differentiations of the powers arise from Śiva's own freedom, not from any external necessity.
items.plain_english: Even the arrangement of their divisions, parts, deficiencies, excesses, and so on is set forth in the scriptures solely by the force of his autonomy.

items.question: In what numerical forms is Bhairava described as unfolding his nature?
premises: Bhairava is described through successive numerical configurations.
These range from one to eight in this verse.
Each configuration names a mode of his manifestation.
items.inference: The one Bhairava freely appears in multiple ordered forms without losing his singular identity.
items.plain_english: He is the single hero, then the paired one, having three powers and a fourfold nature, having five forms, this one with a sixfold nature, adorned as sevenfold and eightfold.

items.question: How does the numerical unfolding of Bhairava culminate in the twelvefold wheel?
premises: The sequence continues through nine, ten, and eleven.
Bhairava is identified as lord of the great twelve-spoked wheel.
This completes the numerical presentation.
items.inference: The unfolding of Bhairava's forms reaches a culminating expression in his lordship over the twelvefold wheel.
items.plain_english: He has a ninefold nature, the power of the ten directions, and an elevenfold nature; thus Bhairava is the lord of the great twelve-spoked wheel.

items.question: How far does the expansion of the Lord's universal wheel extend?
premises: The wheel can be described as thousand-spoked.
It can also be uncountably spoked.
The great Lord expands there as universal power.
items.inference: Bhairava's manifestation in wheels is not limited to fixed numbers but expands boundlessly as universal power.
items.plain_english: Thus, in the wheel of the universe—whether thousand-spoked or even uncountably spoked—the Lord, the great sovereign whose power is the universe, expands.

items.question: How are differences among the many wheels explained without denying their unity?
premises: There are many wheels.
Each follows the nature of its own group.
Their differences are explained through a unity proper to each wheel.
items.inference: Multiplicity among the wheels is a differentiated expression within underlying unities.
items.plain_english: Even among those wheels, the differences belonging to each wheel are explained, case by case, through a unity that follows the nature of its own group.

items.question: How is the Lord described as ruler of six wheels in the Traiśirasa doctrine?
premises: The Traiśirasa doctrine uses a reckoning of four, six, two, and two.
On that basis the Lord is said to rule six wheels.
This belongs to his wondrous own form.
items.inference: Different doctrinal reckonings present the same Lord as sovereign over specific wheel-configurations.
uncertainties: The internal arithmetic of the compound is compressed and tradition-dependent.
items.plain_english: In the Traiśirasa doctrine, by the reckoning of four, six, two, and two, the Lord—whose own form is wondrous—is said to have sovereignty over six wheels.

items.question: How are the names of the wheel goddesses determined in that system?
premises: The wheel goddesses have distinct names.
Their names correspond to differences of function.
They also correspond to gentle or fierce forms, meditations, and etymological meanings.
items.inference: The goddess names are theological designations shaped by function, iconography, meditation, and meaningful etymology.
items.plain_english: There, the names of the goddesses of the wheel are determined according to differences of function and by etymological conception of the yoginīs associated with gentle or fierce forms and meditations.

items.question: What is worshipped as the inner body of the one lord of consciousness?
premises: The one lord of consciousness has an inner body.
That inner body is pratibhā, creative intuition.
It is worshipped as the wheel of waves of consciousness, gentle or otherwise measured.
items.inference: The object of worship is ultimately the inner intuitive body of consciousness itself, appearing as its wave-wheel.
items.plain_english: For the one lord of consciousness, the inner body is indeed creative intuition; as gentle or in another measured form, the wheel of waves of consciousness is worshipped.

items.question: How is the goddess-consciousness nourished through meditation, speech, and outer action?
premises: The intention is that this consciousness may be nourished.
Nourishment comes from meditation mixed with articulate expression.
It also comes from external activity.
items.inference: The goddess-consciousness is strengthened when inner contemplation, expressive speech, and outer practice converge.
items.plain_english: With the intention, 'May this be nourished,' the goddess-consciousness is nourished by such meditation mixed with articulate expression, and also by external activity.

items.question: What result appears when nourished consciousness becomes fully clear?
premises: When nourished, consciousness becomes clear and shines.
It grants a fruit corresponding to that nourishment.
The analogy given is a dry place becoming a clear lake.
items.inference: Clarified consciousness yields a fitting fruition, transforming dryness into lucid plenitude.
uncertainties: The final clause is elliptical and best read through the stated analogy.
items.plain_english: When it becomes clear, it shines and grants him a corresponding fruit. Nourishment is like a dry place becoming a lake; therefore there is clear water.

items.question: How does meditation extend through phonemes that naturally flow with essence?
premises: Meditation follows and becomes centered on that consciousness.
Certain phonemes naturally flow with essence.
These phonemes participate in the extension of meditation.
items.inference: Meditation can be prolonged and embodied through phonemes whose intrinsic resonance carries nourishing essence.
uncertainties: The verse introduces an example completed in the next verse.
items.plain_english: Then, having followed that, meditation centered on it is extended; and there are phonemes which by their own nature flow with essence, as follows.

items.question: How do specific phonemes clarify consciousness by attaining a seed state?
premises: Certain phonemes, especially dental and labial combinations, are used.
Together they attain the state of a seed.
In that seed state they clarify consciousness.
items.inference: Mantric phonemes can function as seed-forms that render consciousness vivid and explicit.
uncertainties: The exact phonetic cluster intended is not specified in the verse itself.
items.plain_english: Those phonemes, mostly dental, labial, and dental, formed together with certain other sounds, attain the state of a seed and make that consciousness clear.
